caveats: EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE. python-docx's 239 items fall into 32 distinct closure file-sets, the largest holding 36 items; CoreShop's 422 fall into 142. Sylius's 1,950 fall into 174, the largest holding 202 -- one step-definition set answers a tenth of that pool, so an item-level interval over Sylius overstates its evidence by more than either v1 project's does. Any interval, variance or significance test over items must resample the CLUSTERS: per-item outcomes inside one cluster move together, because one step-definition module answers every item in it.

INCLUSION THRESHOLD DIFFERS BY PROJECT, and the difference is in `summary.json` for both. CoreShop ships at min_live_steps=3; python-docx at 2. The rule counts a scenario's LIVE STEPS INCLUDING ITS BACKGROUND, and CoreShop's domain scenarios carry a 13-step Background while every python-docx scenario has none — so the same literal 3 is a far stricter rule against a library whose canonical criterion is `Given a blank document / Then ...`. At 3 the docx pool would be 136 items over 29 clusters instead of 239 over 32; both numbers are published, the released threshold is 2, and every excluded item is still listed with its reason. Sylius also ships at 2, like python-docx and unlike CoreShop's 3 -- but 848 of its 855 feature files carry a Background, so its 2 is not python-docx's 2 either. Every project's threshold is in its own summary.json and every excluded item keeps its reason.

THE VACUOUS FLOOR IS A MUTATION NUMBER, NOT A PASS RATE. A stub that defines every step with an empty body PASSES the scenario — that is what makes it the floor worth measuring — so the stub's scenario pass rate is 1.000 (239/239, measured; CoreShop's is 422/422) and discriminates nothing at all. The <= 0.02 gate is over MUTATION RECALL, and the python-docx pair is published with its numerators in release/python-docx/anti_vacuity.json. Gold's 1.000 in that pair is the REFERENCE IDENTITY, not a measurement: the kill set is DEFINED by the same sweep it is scored against, so the number cannot move and cannot catch a flaky item — flakiness is controlled by the N=3 validation legs in release/python-docx/validation.jsonl instead, and the gold side is gated by checks that can fail (sweep completeness, duplicate-freedom, kill-set/manifest consistency). The number to read is the stub's, and the number that says how much there was to detect is gold's kills over the covered pairs.

API SIMILARITY AND COVERAGE ARE INDEPENDENT. python-docx API rows use direct_calls joined to its pinned production method index. Rows collected before the recorder supplied direct_calls remain API-unscored; their per-scenario coverage is scored independently from gold and system lines.

THE DOCX SUBSET IS A CENSUS. `evaldocx32` holds one item from each of the 32 closure clusters, i.e. every representative there is; its sidecar records `census: true` so the seed beside it is not read as evidence of a random draw that never happened.
